subject: Algorithms
title: Discover Bubble Sort
description: Discover how Bubble Sort compares neighboring values and swaps them into order.

mission.title: Sort the Values
mission.description: Compare neighbors and let the largest values bubble to the end.

quiz.question: What does Bubble Sort compare at each step?
options: Only the first and last values
Every value at the same time

discovery.title: Values Bubble Into Place
discovery.summary: Bubble Sort repeatedly compares neighboring values. Larger values swap right until each pass places one value in its final position.

sections.title: What is Bubble Sort?
sections.content: Bubble Sort is a sorting algorithm that repeatedly compares neighboring values.

sections.title: Adjacent comparisons
sections.content: The algorithm looks at two values next to each other and checks whether they are in the correct order.

sections.title: Swapping
sections.content: If the left value is larger, the two values swap positions.

sections.title: Passes
sections.content: One pass moves the largest remaining value to the end of the unsorted area.

sections.title: Time complexity
sections.content: Bubble Sort takes O(n²) time in the typical unsorted case because it may compare many pairs over many passes.

alternate_explanations.title: Think of arranging books
alternate_explanations.content: Imagine arranging books from thinnest to thickest by checking neighbors. Whenever a thicker book is on the left, swap the two books.

alternate_explanations.title: Watch one value move
alternate_explanations.content: Start with [50, 20, 40, 10, 30]. Compare 50 and 20, then swap. Compare 50 and 40, then swap again. The larger 50 keeps moving right during the pass.

introduction.title: Meet Bubble Sort
introduction.content: Bubble Sort puts values in order by comparing neighboring values and swapping them only when they are backwards.
points: It looks at one pair of neighbors at a time.
A larger left value moves right by swapping.
You will watch values gradually reach their final places.

worked_example.title: Watch one swap
worked_example.content: Start with a small unsorted row and compare the first two neighbors.

steps.explanation: 50 is to the left of 20, but it is larger, so this pair is out of order.
Swap the pair so the smaller value moves left and the larger value moves right.
Now compare 50 with its next neighbor. Repeating this is one pass.

worked_example.conclusion: During a pass, large values keep moving right until one reaches its final position.

next.title: Now watch the full array sort.
next.content: Use NEXT STEP to compare each highlighted pair.

action_explanations.compare-adjacent: These two neighbors are the only values Bubble Sort is deciding about right now.
action_explanations.swap: The larger value moved one position right, bringing this pair into order.
action_explanations.continue-pass: Move to the next neighboring pair; the same comparison rule applies again.
action_explanations.complete-pass: One value has bubbled all the way to its final position at the right.
action_explanations.sorted-array: Every pair is now in order, so the whole array is sorted.

challenge.title: Bubble Sort Challenge
challenge.start_message: Move 50 toward its final place by following the comparison rule yourself.
challenge.continue_message: Challenge complete. You can keep using NEXT STEP to finish sorting the array.

phases.title: Fix the first pair
phases.instruction: Compare the first two values and make that pair ordered.

target.label: Goal
target.description: Turn [50] [20] into [20] [50] without changing the third value yet.

phases.feedback: Look at the highlighted neighboring pair and decide whether its left value is larger.

phases.title: Finish 50's first pass
phases.instruction: Keep comparing 50 with the next neighbor until it reaches the far right.

target.label: Goal
target.description: Let the largest value, 50, bubble to the end of the first pass.

phases.feedback: Continue through the adjacent pairs and swap only when the left value is larger.

recall.title: Recall
recall.prompt: In your own words, why does a large value move toward the right during Bubble Sort?
recall.empty_message: Write a short explanation before submitting.
recall.model_answer: Bubble Sort compares neighboring values. When a larger value is on the left, it swaps with the smaller neighbor, so repeated swaps move the larger value right.

guidance.start_message: Complete a small pass. Decide whether the highlighted pair swaps or stays.

items.content: Swap only when the left value is larger than its right neighbor.

phases.title: Complete one comparison
phases.feedback: Compare the two highlighted values before choosing.

guidance.start_message: Sort this array with fewer prompts. Each adjacent pair needs its own decision.

items.content: A KEEP decision is just as important as a SWAP decision.

phases.title: Sort with decisions
phases.instruction: Choose the correct swap decision for every highlighted pair.
phases.feedback: Only swap an out-of-order neighboring pair.

guidance.start_message: Sort the array while tracking comparisons and swaps yourself.

phases.title: Solve the sort
phases.instruction: Sort the complete array without hints.
phases.feedback: Bubble Sort compares neighbors from left to right, pass after pass.

guidance.start_message: This array is randomized. Predict each swap decision with no hints.

phases.title: Master an unfamiliar sort
phases.instruction: Sort the randomized array through correct pair-by-pair decisions.
phases.feedback: Look only at the highlighted neighboring values.

thinking.title: Simulate a Bubble Sort pass
thinking.instruction: Before the array moves, predict the complete first pass.
thinking.do_not_execute: Do not click SWAP or KEEP yet. Work through every pair mentally.

prediction_fields.label: Array after the pass
prediction_fields.prompt: What is the array after this pass?

thinking.replay_message: Now replay the pass one pair at a time.

solve.title: Expert Bubble Sort
solve.instruction: Sort the randomized array with no hints. Accuracy of each comparison is the challenge.
solve.operation_rule: Every highlighted neighboring pair needs one correct SWAP or KEEP decision.
solve.feedback: Do not invent a shortcut: decide the current adjacent pair.
solve.solved_result: The randomized array is sorted through correct Bubble Sort decisions.
